correctness.rationale: With N=2k and the stated face orientations, centering the columns of NI−ssᵀ leaves N(e_i−1_A/k) in one sign block or its counterpart in the other. Their centered (k−1)-spaces are orthogonal. Polar vertices are −(v_i+v_j)/(4k) for opposite-block indices; their common norm gives the inradius, and the vertex norm gives the enclosing radius. The facet normals sum to zero and span, so no larger inball or nonzero equal-radius center is possible. Independent block permutations kill cross terms of invariant quadratic forms, and swapping the blocks equates the two scalar restrictions, proving the ellipsoid assertions by uniqueness. The centroid and the unique Santaló point are fixed by the group. Each of the k² facet cones omits one vertex per block and has the same volume. In the uniform-simplex second moment formula, averaging the sum of vertex outer products retains each vertex with weight 1−1/k; the square of the vertex sum restores weight 1/k, with no cross term. The resulting N² projector divided by (N−1)N gives covariance. The Gram determinant after omitting one vertex per block gives cone volume N^(2k−2)/[k(2k−2)!]; the polar is an orthogonal product of the regular simplex polars, each a reflected rescaling by 1/(4k). These give both volumes, their product and the stated Stirling asymptotic. All claims are intrinsic, for k≥2 and the specific orientation.
